# dsh-telegram-connector

Drive a DeepSeek Harness runtime from Telegram —
same workspaces, same sessions, same tools as the w
eb UI, from your phone.

One **Telegram group per workspace**, one **forum topic per session**. A session
started in the brow

ser can be adopted as a topic with its history (`/sync`); a
session started from the phone is the sa

me session in the browser. There is no
shadow store of conversations: Telegram is a projection of th

in the browser. There is no
shadow store of conversations: Telegram is a projection of the harness.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The full command reference is `docs/COMMANDS.md` — the bot's
`/help <command>` prints the same text,

and every command accepts `--help`. The reasoning
behind the mapping is in `docs/DESIGN.md`; suppor

ted DSH
versions are in `COMPATIBILITY.md`.
## Features

- **Topics are sessions.** Create a topic by hand and start talking, or let the
bot create one per s

ession with `/new`. Topics are never silently re-assigned.
- **Web ↔ phone continuity.** `/sync` ado

pts sessions created in the web UI,
creates a topic for each and replays the tail of the conversatio

n. Renaming
round-trips both ways, and closing a topic archives its session. Archiving
from the web

UI is **not** mirrored: run `/close` for that.
- **Streaming replies.** One message per turn, edited

*tables are rewritten before sending** — a monospaced code block when they
fit, a bullet list when t

hey do not — because not every Telegram client
renders a GFM table. If the API rejects rich content,

an HTML subset takes
over and finally plain text. Splitting is fence- and table-aware.
- **Read and

streaming reactions.** The bot reacts 👀 to a prompt when it reads
it, and ✍ to a reply while it is

still being edited; the streaming reaction is
removed when the turn settles. Media without a caption

is staged and marked
🙉 until a caption or the next text prompt. Change any emoji online with
`/reac

tions` (Telegram's fixed reaction set is validated).
- **Attachments.** Photos, image documents, vid

eos, video notes, audio, voice
notes and animations are downloaded through the Bot API and attached

with
DSH's attachment service. Albums are debounced and attached together; a
captionless upload wait

s for the prompt instead of starting one turn per file.
- **Reply-to reuse.** Reply to an earlier ph

oto/file/video/audio message to
attach it to the new prompt. The referenced message is included as a

quoted
context block; external replies are supported and download errors are surfaced
to the model

so it can suggest a fix.
- **Forwarded messages.** A forwarded message becomes a `Forwarded from …`

context turn; forwarded rich messages are read from `rich_message.blocks`, and
a reply to a forwarde

d message also records its origin in the reference block.
- **Process rows.** Tool calls, host comma

nds and skill loads become short safe
[该节后续省略]

bindings and the plu
gin surface, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Requirements

- A DSH runtime with the `web` profile and the `agents` service (any normal
install). Optional piece

s — workspace registry, session query/title, plugin
manager, the container supervisor — are detected

at runtime, and the features
that need them say so instead of crashing.
- A Telegram bot from @BotF

ather.
- A group with **Topics enabled** and the bot as **admin** with *Manage Topics*
(plus *Change

Info* if you want group title sync).
- **Privacy mode off** for the bot (BotFather → `/setprivacy`

→ Disable).
Otherwise it cannot see plain messages in topics, which is the entire input
path.
- One
running instance per bot token: a single long-poll loop.

Bots cannot create groups or enable Topics, so `workspace new` prints a
one-tap `?startgroup=` link
— you create the group, the bot binds it.
## Install

The supported path is the setup repository, which installs the runtime, this
connector at the matchi

ng tag, and a supervisor that can restart it from
Telegram:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`./install.sh --check` prints the whole plan and changes nothing. The setup
pins a recommended conne

ctor tag in its `plugins.json`; the connector is
[该节后续省略]
## Security

- `allowedUserIds` is the gate for **using** the bot, and `adminUserId` is the
gate for changing the

deployment (`/system restart|update|rollback`, plugin
mutations, `/workspace` and `/bind`). An empt

y allowlist means nobody, not
everybody. When `adminUserId` is unset, the control-chat owner is admi

n, and
otherwise any allowlisted user can run admin commands.
- The bot token comes from the environ

ment; `cordis.patch.yml` never carries it.
- The bot is an admin of its groups and can delete topics

. `/dangerous cleanup`
requires an explicit `confirm`; `/forget` never deletes anything.
- **Plugins

execute host code.** `/plugins add` inspects first and installs only
after **Confirm** (or `/plugin

s confirm`); blocked install scripts need `/plugins approve`, which
names exactly the packages allow

ed. The connector refuses to remove or disable
itself, since that would cut the line mid-command.
-
`bindings.json` contains chat ids and session ids, not message contents.
